explain.say: Each ridge branches into stacked shelves spaced about two hundred millionths of a millimetre apart. Light reflects off every shelf, and at that spacing the blue waves line up and add together while other colours cancel.

explain.say: Colour made by tiny shapes instead of pigment is called structural colour. It shifts as you change your viewing angle, which is called iridescence, and peacock feathers and jewel beetles use it too.

faq.a: Structural colour is colour made by tiny structures that bounce light so that some colours add up and others cancel. It needs no pigment, and it often shimmers and changes with angle.
asks: How can colour come without pigment?

faq.q: Why do the wings change colour when they move?
faq.a: The colour depends on the angle between the light, the scales and your eye. As the wing moves, that angle changes, so the colour shifts. This shimmer is called iridescence.

faq.q: What happens if you crush a morpho wing scale?
faq.a: Crushing destroys the tiny shelves that make the colour, so the blue disappears and you are left with dull brown dust. With pigment colour, crushing would not change the colour.
asks: What colour is a crushed butterfly wing?

faq.q: Why do peacock feathers change colour?
faq.a: Peacock feathers contain tiny regular patterns of melanin rods. Their spacing makes certain colours, like blue and green, add up, so the feathers shimmer as the angle changes.
asks: How do peacocks get their colours?

faq.q: Why would a butterfly want to be shiny blue?
faq.a: Flashes of blue help males signal to rivals and mates, and the on-off flashing as the wings beat can confuse predators. The undersides are dull brown for camouflage when resting.
asks: What is the underside of a morpho wing like?

facts: Blue morpho butterflies have no blue pigment; their colour comes from nanostructures on their wing scales.
Peacock feathers, jewel beetles and many hummingbirds also use structural colour.

quiz.say: A blue morpho wing scale is crushed into powder. What colour is the powder?
quiz.why: The blue comes from tiny structures, not pigment. Crushing them destroys the structure, so the blue disappears.

wrong.0: There is no blue pigment to keep the colour.
wrong.2: Without the regular structure, no colours are boosted.
